messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alice: P0 - traffic spike + increased tail latency on sequencer after recent feature flip. See https://internal/ops/incidents/6765432109 :rotating_light:

alice: seeing 4xx/504s at the edge and queued requests building on canary nodes. Digging into sequencer logs now.

sasha: I can take traffic routing - pausing canary to 0% immediately, shifting 50% -> fallback pool. Will update LB. :thumbsup:

david: adding context: the flip enabled the "sequencer_v2" path which changes batch commit ordering. We rolled remotes at 03:12Z. Kernel fallback notices started ~03:15Z.

emma: customer-support FYI, we have elevated errors on /v1/generate for a subset of customers (mostly mid-size tenants). Possible request reordering.

alice: quick mitigation plan: 1) flip featureflag sequencer_v2 -> off (kill-switch) 2) rollback canary release if flag flip doesn't immediately reduce errors 3) gather a short CPU/latency diff and hand off to runtime team for root cause.

sasha: running: `redwood featureflip set sequencer_v2 off --env=prod --scope=canary` -> command returned 202. Pushing full rollout pause via release-bot.

release-bot: Release action: paused rollout wave-275. Canary traffic set to 0% at 03:21:10Z.

emma: customer-support: initial customer triage: ~12 customers reporting timeouts, 3 with business-impacting errors. Communicating we have mitigation in flight.

david: logs showing frequent kernel fallback on GPUs with messages: `KV cache miss -> falling back to seq-exec`. Batching windows look smaller than expected; latency variance spiking.

alice: monitoring: latency p50 -> +40ms, p95 -> +420ms, 99th -> +1.2s on affected routes. Error rate for canary nodes jumped from 0.3% -> 3.8%.

maria: starting rollback of the canary release (wave-275) to previous artifact: `release rollback wave-275 --target=wave-274` (initiated). ETA for completion ~4 mins.

sasha: traffic shift executed: 50% of canary traffic -> fallback pool completed at 03:23:05Z. Observing preliminary drop in 5xxs.

emma: customer-support: letting customers know we paused rollout and rolled back; telling impacted customers we'll follow up with RCA in 24h.

david: reproduction notes: small inputs with high concurrency triggered an ordering path that increases KV cache churn; when churn hits threshold kernel selector falls back to safer but slower exec path -> sawtooth latency. Suspect selector heuristics change in v2.

alice: rollback completed at 03:26:09Z. Post-rollback metrics: error rate down to 0.6%, p95 back to baseline-ish (+60ms delta). Keeping paged oncall until stable for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1432. Severity: P0. Handoff to eng-runtime oncall (sasha) for postmortem and root cause.

sasha: grabbed it. Next steps: collect kernel-selection traces, KV-cache stats, and batching histograms for the 03:10-03:30Z window. Will coordinate with runtime team and release to prepare a safer feature flip plan.

emma: customer-support: all affected customers notified. Logged follow-ups in CS ticket CS-9876 and linked to the incident.

alice: note for postmortem: consider feature gating the sequencer_v2 path on per-tenant basis and add canary smoke tests that simulate high-concurrency short-input workloads.

david: also propose an automated circuit breaker in kernel selector to avoid thrashing between paths during transient cache churn.

sasha: acknowledged. Will schedule an on-call deep-dive in 45m and assign owners for fixes.

emma: thanks all — closing the urgent loop for now. Keep channel updates light unless any regression. :white_check_mark:
